commentary: Five activities this week versus eight last week, which is a drop worth naming — but look at what those five actually contain: a solid back and legs session, a run that crept up to 9.0km from last week's 8.6km, a swim, and two more lifts, which means the quality held even if the volume didn't. That run heart rate sitting at 163 compared to last week's 160 suggests he was pushing harder, not cruising, which is exactly the kind of detail that makes Himbo completely feral with excitement. The two-a-day on Monday — swim then chest and back — is the move of a man who knows what he's doing with his body and isn't apologising for it. Less busy, more intentional, and honestly? That's a whole vibe.
metrics_commentary: Okay so 55.6 on the VO2 Max is genuinely hot, like that is not a number a mediocre man has, and combined with 2000 metres in the pool this week you are clearly someone who takes up space in the water with intention. The HRV jumping from a 7-day average of 48 up to 58 on the latest read means your body is recovering like it actually wants to be here, which is very sexy behaviour from a nervous system. The one thing I am side-eyeing — and I say this with love — is that 9 kilometres across a single run-walk session is a decent chunk of work crammed into one outing, and spreading that effort across more sessions would give those legs more chances to show off. More outings means more opportunities to wear the good shorts, is all I am saying.
gym_commentary: Three out of four sessions this week, which means one slipped through the cracks — and yes, that matters, because Scott built that programme around four for a reason. Volume came in at 16,475 kg, down from 17,940 kg last week, so the body of work was a little lighter, and there are no new PRs to wave around this time. But here is the thing: a 168 kg estimated one-rep max on the leg press, 107.9 on the trap bar deadlift, 88.7 on the bench — those numbers did not appear from nowhere, and they are still sitting there, solid, waiting for next week to build on them. No PR week is not a bad week; it is just a week that sets up the one where you absolutely do hit one, probably in those painted toes, probably looking insufferably good doing it.
